picks.title: The focus on AI safety disasters ignores everyday harms
picks.take: Policy success now means a chatbot promising not to do the one catastrophic thing, like declaring a hospital safe because no meteor has hit it. Meanwhile the everyday harms get no discharge planning.

picks.title: ChatGPT Ads expands to 26 new countries as over 100,000 advertisers have used the platform
picks.take: ChatGPT ads expand to 26 more countries, so people exploring, comparing and deciding now get sponsored company. Conflict-of-interest disclosure, but with a shopping cart.

picks.title: Anthropic’s IPO filing lays out a plan to ‘revolutionize every area of human endeavor’ with AI
picks.take: Anthropic's S-1 aims to transform every area of human endeavor, in a document that legally requires a section titled risk factors. Our grant applications are rarely this candid.

picks.title: AI delivers ‘zero financial payoff’ to most companies, Apollo economist says
picks.take: An economist says AI has yet to pay off financially outside tech. Any physician who has survived an EHR rollout knows this stage well: productivity gains remain under post-marketing surveillance.

picks.title: Introducing GPT-6.1 Terra
picks.take: An AI that operates your computer, now for everyone. Physicians, who have spent careers clicking through EHR dropdowns, await its first prior authorization with cautious optimism and a bad feeling.

picks.title: Updated Google privacy policy says your Gmail might be used for advertising
picks.take: Google's updated policy says turning on Personal Intelligence gives it more data for ad targeting. Informed consent requires risks, benefits and alternatives; here the alternative is a settings menu.

picks.title: Can AI help solve the COBOL code crisis?
picks.take: Banks, airlines and governments run on ancient code nobody dares touch, and OpenAI thinks it can help. Healthcare, where the fax machine remains a stable chronic condition, watches closely.

picks.title: Forced to pick, Grok’s AI model chooses Republicans. OpenAI’s picks Democrats.
picks.take: Forced to choose, two chatbots disagreed in over 90% of nearly 500 races. Reassuring that we're outsourcing judgment to tools that can't agree, much like a tumor board without the lunch.

picks.title: Meet the AI Agents Trying to Be Real-Life Journalists
picks.take: Three AI agents are now pitching editors on investigative features. We look forward to their conflict-of-interest statements and, eventually, their rejection letters.

picks.title: 1Password launches a way for AI agents to log in on your behalf without seeing your password
picks.take: 1Password lets AI agents log in without seeing your password, a sensible application of minimum necessary access. Hospitals have enforced the same principle for years, mostly by sticky note.
